question: Which acid and its salts are widely used as food preservatives to prevent the growth of mould, yeast and fungi?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sorbic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sorbic acid** and its salts, such as potassium sorbate, are widely used as **food preservatives** to prevent the growth of **mould, yeast, and fungi**.
 
• Sorbic acid is a naturally occurring compound first isolated from the berries of the **rowan tree (Sorbus aucuparia)** in 1859.
 
• It is effective in low concentrations and is commonly used in **processed foods, beverages, and bakery products** to maintain quality and safety.
 
• Sorbic acid has **antifungal properties** and inhibits microbial growth by interfering with the metabolic processes of fungi and yeast.
 
• Due to its **low toxicity** and safety for human consumption, sorbic acid is approved by food safety authorities worldwide, including the **US FDA** and the **European Food Safety Authority (EFSA)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Perchloric Acid:**

 
 
• **Perchloric acid** is a strong mineral acid primarily used in industrial and laboratory applications.
 
• It is not used as a food preservative due to its corrosive and highly reactive properties.
 
• Applications include **oxidation reactions** and the preparation of perchlorate salts.
 
 
 
• **Boric Acid:**
 
 
• **Boric acid** is a weak acid with applications in antiseptics, insecticides, and industrial products.
 
• It is not a primary food preservative due to concerns about its **toxicity** when ingested in large amounts.
 
• Boric acid is used in small amounts as a pH buffer in some industrial food preparation processes.
 
 
 
• **Malic Acid:**
 
 
• **Malic acid** is a naturally occurring organic acid found in fruits such as apples and cherries.
 
• It is primarily used in the food and beverage industry as a **flavor enhancer** and acidulant.
 
• While it contributes to the tangy taste of foods, it does not have **antimicrobial properties** like sorbic acid.
 
 
 
• **Sorbic Acid:**
 
 
• Sorbic acid is widely used in foods such as **cheese, wine, dried fruits, and soft drinks**.
 
• Potassium sorbate, a salt of sorbic acid, is highly soluble and often preferred for use in liquid products.
 
• It is effective in **acidic environments**, making it suitable for preserving acidic foods like fruit juices.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sorbic Acid:**
 
 
• Used in **pharmaceuticals** to prevent microbial contamination of medicines.
 
• Commonly used in **cosmetics** to extend the shelf life of products by preventing microbial growth.
 
• Acts as an antifungal agent in food packaging materials.
